messages:
Maria G: Heads-up — preparing a private/on-prem proof for a customer that needs near-zero telemetry egress. Question: what is the absolute minimal set of signals we need to keep for RBAC/audit/KMS rotation without compromising incident response?

Kevin O: Minimal = auth events, role/user changes, API key lifecycle, and KMS key-ops (encrypt/decrypt/sign). Everything else can be local-only. :thumbsup:

Maria G: For KMS key-ops, do we need full request bodies or just metadata? Customer will reject any payload leakage.

Kevin O: Metadata only. Record: timestamp, principal, operation, key-id, outcome, and size/hash of payload (sha256). No plaintext, no prompt/content. Example log line: `2026-02-28T12:03:22Z principal=svc-redwood-app op=Decrypt key=proj-123 result=OK hash=sha256:aa12...`

Jordan P: Agree. Practically we should expose a config toggle: telemetry.mode = [none, minimal, full]. For private/airgap default should be `minimal` and enforce via policy.

Maria G: Any objections to keeping stack traces locally but shipping only an opaque support bundle on request? Customer wants no automatic outbound.

Ops Lead: That’s the pattern we use for Dedicated already. Signed support bundles only, uploaded by the customer or via an agent that requires an explicit approval token. Support flow: operator creates a one-time signed token, customer pastes into the UI to allow upload.

sec-bot: SECURITY ALERT: Note the requirement for HSM-backed key material for remote-rotate workflows. See RFC: /docs/sec/hsm-rotations.md (internal). :eyes:

Kevin O: For remote support we should provide an ephemeral support key pattern. Steps: generate support key in HSM, scope to single operation, TTL 5m, auditable and auto-revoked. No persistent export of private key allowed.

Jordan P: Network policy side — recommend default deny egress in k8s + explicit egress for NTP, DNS, and local cargo (if using image mirrors). If customer forbids all egress, show a graceful degraded mode for telemetry and support. Example k8sNetworkPolicy snippet to allow DNS+NTP only:

```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-dns-ntp-egress
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector: {} # cluster DNS
    ports:
    - protocol: UDP
      port: 53
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 0.0.0.0/0
    ports:
    - protocol: UDP
      port: 123
```

Maria G: For compliance, auditors want immutable audit logs. Options: local WORM filesystem + periodic signed digests that the customer OR Redwood stores. Which do we prefer?

Kevin O: Signed digests are good. Implement log rotation: compress -> sign with HSM -> store locally + export digest if allowed. Export should be one-way and only include hashes, timestamps, and signature. No raw log egress without explicit approval.

Jordan P: Vulnerability triage: in an airgapped/private deployment we must avoid automatic CVE telemetry. Instead implement a local scan tool that produces a signed findings bundle. Customer can choose to share it. For critical CVEs we still want alerting — propose an opt-in emergency callback channel that only sends metadata and requires multi-party approval.

Ops Lead: Incident response playbook notes:
- If customer permits outbound (minimal): we get auth+audit+metrics (no payload).
- If strict no-egress: require customer to run support-runbook locally and produce signed debug bundle.
- In both cases: require RBAC change audits before any remote action.

Maria G: One operational question — KMS rotation. Can we automate rotation without touching customer key material? The ask: Redwood triggers rotation but key never leaves HSM.

Kevin O: Yes. Use a Wrap/Unwrap model where our service issues a rotation operation that calls into the local KMS/HSM via an API. All operations are logged locally. We need a handshake: rotation-req signed by Redwood operator key and validated inside customer HSM. No material export.

sec-bot: REMINDER: Make sure to document RBAC roles used by support: `support-read`, `support-bundle-create`, `support-remote-op`. Least privilege enforced.

Jordan P: Quick UX ask — surface telemetry.mode in console header and disable any toggles when running in airgapped packaging. Prevent accidental enable.

Maria G: Sounds good. Action items: Kevin to draft minimal audit schema + log signing flow; Jordan to add network policy examples and emergency callback opt-in; Ops Lead to write support bundle onboarding flow. I'll consolidate into an RFC for private-deploy security. :rocket:

Kevin O: Will do. Draft expected EOD tomorrow.

Ops Lead: Adding a runbook entry for incident escalation and who can approve support bundles.
